source.edition: Elementary Topology, Michael C. Gemignani, Second Edition
source.boundsConvention: Normalized [x,y,width,height] around graphics and labels, excluding captions and prose.

verification.visualReview: Full source pages and final vector renderings inspected; compared at equal crop scale. The U label opening was adjusted after comparison.

figures.mathematics: A finite strictly increasing partition x0=a<…<xn=b belongs to the family of all partitions of [a,b]. The source places finer partitions first in its order; that convention is retained explicitly.
figures.visual: Bracketed endpoints, dashed line continuations, x1/x2/x3/x(n−1) point marks, a=x0 and b=xn above, and a gray three-dot ellipsis retain the source arrangement.
limits: The default Substance supplies one explicit finite partition; the ellipsis hides actual intermediate indices and does not assert a finite representation of the entire directed family.
Clean vector type and strokes replace scanned lettering; the source-defined partition order is not silently reversed.

figures.mathematics: For distinct unseparable x,y in a non-T2 space, the directed product of their neighborhood systems indexes a selector choosing s(U,V) in every U∩V; its net converges to both x and y. The drawn value is one witness distinct from this all-neighborhood hypothesis.
figures.visual: Overlapping unequal oval neighborhoods U,V, three point marks x/y/s(U,V), and the opening in U at the selected-value label match the source. Pale orange transparency distinguishes the neighborhoods and overlap.
limits: Neighborhood outlines are a schematic view; the Substance assigns no Euclidean metric or plane coordinates to X.
The all-neighborhood selection property is declared as a mathematical hypothesis, not inferred from the one depicted value.
